**Implementation** in `dominoes.py`: `can_chain` uses backtracking search — it tries each domino (in either orientation) as the first stone, then recursively appends remaining dominoes whose left half matches the current right half, checking that the chain closes (last right half equals first left half) when all stones are used. It returns the chain as a list of tuples, or `None` when no closed chain exists. Empty input returns `[]`.

This handles the tricky cases in the spec: reversing individual dominoes, backtracking past dead ends (`test_need_backtrack`), and correctly rejecting inputs made of separate disconnected loops.
